evidence.claim: Daily Mail apologized to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, withdrew its corruption allegation, and removed the article that had accused him of stealing British foreign aid money.

evidence.period_fit: Published in the target year and directly relevant to Sharif's public integrity record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Shehbaz as the subject of the withdrawn allegation and apology.
contrary_evidence: The apology concerns a 2019 article, so it is retrospective vindication rather than evidence of a 2022 affirmative act of honesty.
It does not by itself prove full integrity across all domains.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister and tasked him with arresting the economic spiral and restarting IMF talks.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new finance minister faces tight time frame to tackle crises
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister and tasked him with arresting the economic spiral and restarting IMF talks.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the appointment is attributed to Sharif as prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The source also notes Ismail had a close relationship with Sharif, so the appointment is not purely technocratic.
A single professional appointment does not establish a generally merit-based cabinet.

evidence.title: Ishaq Dar appointed federal finance and revenue minister
evidence.excerpt: PML-N stalwart Ishaq Dar was nominated by Nawaz Sharif and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during a meeting and then appointed finance minister on the prime minister's advice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a senior cabinet appointment with named nominators and the official appointment basis.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year and directly tied to Sharif's cabinet decisions.

contrary_evidence: Dar was a seasoned finance professional, so the appointment also had competence credentials.
The party-network nature of the decision still raises a favoritism concern even if the appointee was qualified.

evidence.claim: Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet made up of former rivals, and the cabinet included five women while Miftah Ismail was given the finance portfolio to stabilize the economy.
evidence.title: Pakistan's new PM picks coalition cabinet after Khan ousted

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters feed on the cabinet formation is reliable for the fact of a coalition cabinet and the named composition, though it is still a news report rather than an official gazette.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year at the start of the Sharif government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Shehbaz Sharif as prime minister assembling the cabinet, though coalition bargaining constrained selection.
contrary_evidence: Coalition composition is not the same as integrity, and some posts still reflected party bargaining.
This source is more context than proof of ethical restraint.

evidence.claim: Sharif said the government would prioritize economic stability, support middle and poor households, raise domestic production and agriculture, and improve exports and ease of doing business.

evidence.excerpt: Sharif said the government would prioritize economic stability, support middle and poor households, raise domestic production and agriculture, and improve exports and ease of doing business.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with a clear policy program and target groups.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the statement is Sharif's own policy framing in office.
contrary_evidence: This is a declared program, not proof of delivery.
The speech also blames the predecessor government, so some of the framing is adversarial.

evidence.claim: The government said it had implemented a Rs2,000 monthly cash transfer for families with income below Rs40,000 from June 2022 and would add about 60 million more people to BISP.
evidence.title: Budget Speech 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The government said it had implemented a Rs2,000 monthly cash transfer for families with income below Rs40,000 from June 2022 and would add about 60 million more people to BISP.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with a specific cash-transfer policy, start date, and scale.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sharif as prime minister announcing and incorporating the measure into the coalition budget.
contrary_evidence: The claim is programmatic and self-reported, not an independent disbursement audit.
It reflects relief and cushioning more than broad productivity reform.

evidence.claim: The budget raised BISP funding from Rs250 billion to Rs364 billion, projected access for nine million families under Kafalat, expanded educational scholarships to 10 million students, extended Nashonuma nutrition coverage, and increased Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal support for the poor.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget summary with explicit allocations and beneficiary targets.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared but meaningful: this is the federal budget under Sharif's premiership, though delivery would depend on implementing agencies.
contrary_evidence: Allocated amounts and target counts do not prove actual completion in 2022.
These are social-protection commitments inside a fiscally stressed budget.

evidence.claim: The budget framework defined BISP's goal as a nationwide safety net with effective and transparent targeting and delivery mechanisms, and tied it to concrete outputs including unconditional cash transfers, emergency cash transfers, Waseela-e-Taleem, NSER, and Nashonuma.

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary performance-budget document that links funding to goals and named delivery mechanisms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution: this is a federal performance-budget architecture under Sharif's government, not a personal PM audit of each program arm.
contrary_evidence: This shows institutional design more than realized outcomes.
Performance targets can be aspirational rather than achieved.

evidence.claim: The Public Sector Development Programme was presented as the main instrument for improving socio-economic conditions and achieving government targets, with the 2022-23 budget laying out PSDP size and special packages and relief.

evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the PSDP framework is a government choice under Sharif, though execution would sit with multiple ministries and provinces.
contrary_evidence: The document explains planning, not completed implementation.
Large development allocations do not ensure project delivery under crisis conditions.

evidence.excerpt: Finance Minister Miftah Ismail said Pakistan would cut expenditures and development funds and do belt tightening to revive the IMF programme.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete fiscal-adaptation decision is strong and specific, even when syndicated through a secondary site.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but real: this reflects the Sharif government's economic response through its finance minister.
contrary_evidence: Cutting development funds can also indicate weakness or austerity under duress.
The statement is about intended fiscal correction, not guaranteed recovery.

evidence.claim: Court papers from the NCA investigation say Aneel Mussarat bought a London property on behalf of Shehbaz Sharif and helped buy two others, and that Sharif's lawyers told the NCA the purchases were made on his behalf.
